name: Lemuel Glasgow

probability.label: Uncertain/speculative · 15%
probability.basis: Caleb Glasgow-363 is selected as the very uncertain working father of Lemuel Glasgow-2581. The case combines a local surname household, a compatible older generation and the same Currituck–Pasquotank setting. Lemuel’s November 1833 pension declaration says he was born in Currituck, moved to Pasquotank as an infant and remained there until moving to Randolph about 1803. William Glasgow-428’s previously reviewed 1746 Currituck will names a son Caleb. The two modern Caleb accounts, Glasgow-363 and Glasgow-830, both cite a Pasquotank will of 1803. These details make the established local Caleb family a useful preferred home for Lemuel over an otherwise unidentified father. They do not put Caleb in Lemuel’s infant household or name his parents. The preference for Glasgow-363 is generational: its circa 1726 birth allows a father aged about 27 in 1753; Glasgow-830’s circa 1740 birth would give about 13. Neither Caleb birth is established by a birth record here, and Lemuel himself said he had no age record and only believed he was born in 1753. The younger estimate therefore lowers the second account’s preference without excluding it. No baptism, guardianship, deed or pension statement names Caleb as Lemuel’s father. A collateral connection to Caleb, another local Glasgow father or an unrelated Glasgow immigrant remains possible. This is a low-confidence named-family hypothesis, not a documented father clause.

wikitree_update_summary: Review the very uncertain Lemuel–Caleb father hypothesis, the alternative Caleb account and conflicting chronology/will identity; retain all earlier sources and family links. No mother, merge or confidence upgrade.
